Concomitant administration of NURTEC ODT with strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 results in a significant increase in rimegepant exposure.

There are no adequate data on the developmental risk associated with the use of NURTEC ODT in pregnant women. In animal studies, oral administration of rimegepant during organogenesis resulted in adverse effects on development in rats (decreased fetal body weight and increased incidence of skeletal variations) at exposures greater than those used clinically

tier.note: No adequate human pregnancy data; animal developmental effects occurred in rats only at maternally toxic exposures (>45x human MRHD AUC).

pregnancy_pk.value: No adequate human pregnancy data; animal developmental toxicity in rats occurred only at maternally toxic exposures (no-effect dose ~45x human MRHD AUC).

refs.quote: Plasma exposures (AUC) at the no-effect dose (60 mg/kg/day) for adverse effects on embryofetal development were approximately 45 times that in humans at the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) of 75 mg/day.

A lactation study was conducted, and the results have established a relative infant dose of less than 1% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose and the milk-to-plasma ratio of 0.20 (see Data ) . These data support that transfer of rimegepant into breastmilk is low.

lactation_summary.value: Low transfer into human milk (relative infant dose < 1%; milk-to-plasma ratio 0.20); no data on effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Weigh breastfeeding benefits against maternal clinical need.

refs.quote: There are no data on the effects of rimegepant on a breastfed infant or on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for NURTEC ODT and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from NURTEC ODT or from the underlying maternal condition.

value.effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors substantially increase rimegepant systemic exposure, increasing risk of adverse events.
value.management: Avoid concomitant administration of rimegepant with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

refs.quote: Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Avoid concomitant administration.

value.effect: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibition elevates rimegepant concentrations.
value.management: Avoid another dose of rimegepant within 48 hours when administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor.

value.management: Avoid concomitant administration of rimegepant with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers.

value.effect: Potent P-glycoprotein inhibition increases rimegepant absorption and exposure.
value.management: Avoid another dose of rimegepant within 48 hours when coadministered with a potent P-gp inhibitor.
